best_for: JavaScript and TypeScript developers on Windows, macOS or Linux who want testing, debugging and Git built in, not assembled from plugins.

points.title: Free for non-commercial use
points.text: JetBrains states WebStorm is free for non-commercial use. Commercial use comes with a 30-day free trial, and the page we read does not give the paid price.

points.title: Built in, not plugins
points.text: Code completion, inspections, safe refactoring, a debugger for JavaScript and Node.js, test runners for Jest, Mocha and Vitest, a terminal, Docker and Git are included. React, Angular, Vue, Next.js and Node.js are preconfigured.

points.title: Database tools are included
points.text: SQL and database tools ship with WebStorm at no extra cost, so a separate database client is optional.

points.title: AI is a paid add-on
points.text: The AI Assistant is marked as paid on the features page, so the free licence does not include it.

points.title: Other editors' habits
points.text: VS Code and Sublime keymaps and the IdeaVim plugin from the JetBrains Marketplace let people carry their key habits over.

points.title: Windows has two installers
points.text: Windows gets a per-user and a machine-wide installer, and the machine-wide one needs elevation. Both come in x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Versions run apart by platform
points.text: At the time of checking, JetBrains' download page offered 2026.3, while the Windows entry in the winget listing was still 2026.2.4. Check the version before assuming the platforms match.
